name: Battle on the Ice

phases.title: The two armies stand on the lake
phases.text: Alexander and the men of Novgorod drew up their forces by the lake. The crusaders stood opposite, ready to ride at them. The wings were part of Alexander's army.

phases.title: The crusaders charge across the lake
phases.text: The knights and crusaders charged across the lake and reached the enemy. The chronicle of Novgorod says they drove themselves like a wedge through the Rus' army.

phases.title: The militia holds them up
phases.text: The infantry of the Novgorodian militia held up the charge and its momentum slowed. For a little more than two hours the two sides fought at close quarters on the frozen surface.

phases.title: Alexander sends in the wings
phases.text: After a little more than two hours Alexander ordered the left and right wings of his army, cavalry among them, into the battle. The crusaders were by then exhausted from the struggle on the slippery ice.

phases.title: The crusaders fall back in disarray
phases.text: The crusaders started to retreat in disarray, deeper onto the ice, with the fresh Novgorod cavalry now facing them.

phases.title: The retreat becomes a panic
phases.text: The appearance of the fresh Novgorod cavalry made the crusaders retreat in panic. The Novgorod First Chronicle says the fighting went on during the pursuit, seven versts short of the Subol shore.

note: The plan follows the scholarly reconstruction of the accounts. The accounts do not say which way each army faced, where on the lake the fight took place, or where the wings stood before they entered the battle; the wings are placed on either side of the militia by judgement. Earlier accounts say only that the Rus' and the crusaders fought and that the crusaders were pursued, and the claim of a fight on the ice itself first appears in a later text. Numbers are not shown on the plan.
